final_interpretation: Strict split conformal did not outperform the native intervals because the native Gaussian and Student-t intervals were already close to their target coverage on test, while calibration produced positive additive q-hat values under a descriptively different error distribution. The one-sided additive correction can only widen intervals, so it moved test coverage into overcoverage and increased width; severity conditioning changed bin-specific q-hat values but had negligible aggregate impact and did not repair the worst-bin trade-off. This is a mechanism diagnosis, not an exchangeability or significance claim.
